Launch the CodingManageR Shiny Application (Backward-Compatible Wrapper)

Source: R/app.R
run_app.Rd

Constructs and returns a shiny.appobj configured automatically for either pooled MySQL/MariaDB storage (when MySQL credentials are supplied) or local single-user SQLite storage (with automatic fallback).

Usage

run_app(
  sqlite_path = NULL,
  config = NULL,
  empty = TRUE,
  max_upload_size_gb = 3,
  options = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

sqlite_path

Optional file path to a local SQLite database. Passing a different .sqlite path creates or reopens a separate, isolated project; the parent directory must already exist.

config

Optional named list of database configuration parameters passed to get_db_pool().

empty

Logical passed to seed_initial_data() when initializing a fresh database. Defaults to TRUE (creates only the default admin and historic_user accounts). When FALSE, demonstration data is only inserted into a brand-new, empty database; existing SQLite files or databases that already contain rows are left untouched and trigger a warning.

max_upload_size_gb

Positive numeric maximum file upload size in gigabytes applied via options(shiny.maxRequestSize = ...) while the app runs (restored cleanly on app shutdown). Defaults to 3 (3 GB). Set to NULL to leave the session's existing shiny.maxRequestSize option unchanged.

options

Optional list of options forwarded to shiny::shinyApp().

...

Additional arguments forwarded to shiny::shinyApp().

Value

A shiny.appobj object that launches the Shiny portal when printed or returned from app.R.

Details

For new scripts and deployments, prefer the explicit entrypoints run_app_local() (minimal local SQLite launcher) and run_app_server() (strict MySQL/MariaDB server launcher without SQLite fallback). run_app() is retained for full backward compatibility with existing code.

See also

run_app_local(), run_app_server()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Preferred explicit launchers:
run_app_local(sqlite_path = "study_a.sqlite")
run_app_server()

# Backward-compatible wrapper:
app <- run_app(sqlite_path = tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"), empty = FALSE)
app
} # }
